text:
maria: Heads up — migrating vectorizer-staging to the new helm chart with vault-agent sidecar. After deploy, pods boot but vault-agent fails to unwrap key: KMS Decrypt = AccessDenied. IRSA annotation is present on the pod, and TF created the role + key grant. Any quick checks before I dig deeper?
jon: Quick q — can the pod actually assume the role at runtime? try `kubectl exec` into an app pod and `aws sts get-caller-identity` from the sidecar container.
sam: Also check the KMS grant principal shape. We had a gotcha where session tags / SourceIdentity prevented Decrypt. Did you use session tags or source identity in the grant condition?
maria: Good call — I can see the pod's AWS creds are the role: `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/k8s-vault-agent/i-...` from the sidecar logs. But KMS returns AccessDenied. Logs: `kms:Decrypt failed; user arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/k8s-vault-agent/i-... is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh`.
jon: Common misorders: 1) key policy must allow the root/grantee to create grants, 2) aws_kms_grant needs the exact principal (often the role's ARN, not assumed-role ARN). We usually set grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.k8s_vault_agent.arn (the role, not session).
sam: Past incident: if you used `aws:SourceIdentity` or `aws:PrincipalTag` in KMS key policy/conditions, the assumed-role session identity must match. IRSA sets `sts:SourceIdentity` when using `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` if you pass `TagSpecifications` or session tags. Helm chart might not.
infra-bot: helm deploy finished: chart "vectorizer" v2.3.0 -> failed hooks: post-install (vault-agent). 
jon: Here's a minimal Terraform snippet that worked for us (use role ARN as grantee_principal and allow decrypt):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vault_agent_decrypt" {
  name             = "vault-agent-decrypt"
  key_id           = aws_kms_key.vectorizer_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.k8s_vault_agent.arn
  operations       = ["Decrypt"]
  retiring_principal = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"
}
```
sam: If you need key policy changes instead of grants (some cross-account setups require it), add a KeyPolicy statement like: `Principal: {AWS: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/k8s-vault-agent"}` with `kms:Decrypt`.
maria: We used a grant initially. TF shows aws_kms_grant created, grantee_principal = "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/k8s-vault-agent/i-..." — oh. I probably wired the wrong value by using `data.aws_iam_role.current_session.arn` in a script.
jon: Yup that's the root cause — grants must reference the principal (role ARN), not the assumed role session ARN. Change to role ARN. For IRSA pods the role resource is `aws_iam_role.k8s_vault_agent.arn` in TF.
sam: Also check for `Condition` on the grant/key policy that references `aws:username` or `aws:sourceIdentity`. If you want to lock to pods, prefer checking `sts:SourceIdentity` which map to the kubernetes service account name when you set `sts:SourceIdentity` on the assume-role call. IRSA by default sets `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation and does not set source identity unless you configure it.
maria: Nice catch. I'll patch TF and reapply. Quick question — is it safe to add an allow for Decrypt to the role directly in the key policy instead of a grant? We have cross-account ingest that also needs access.
on: (typo jon should respond) jon: Either works; key policy is more permanent and required for cross-account. Grants are ephemeral and easier to rotate. For cross-account you can put a Condition limiting the principal to the role ARN and optionally `aws:SourceIp` or `aws:PrincipalOrgID`.
helm-bot: hook "vault-agent-postinstall" failed: 1 error(s) occurred.
maria: Applied TF fix: swapped grantee_principal to role ARN, re-created aws_kms_grant. Re-deploying helm now.
infra-bot: pod vectorizer-7d6b9 vault-agent: fetching wrapped key... success.
maria: Confirmed — vault-agent unwrapped the key and started talking to Vault. Thanks all! :tada: I'll follow up with a short note in the infra playbook about not using assumed-role ARNs in KMS grants.
jon: Nice. Add a tiny TF test in CI to ensure `aws_kms_grant.grantee_principal` doesn't contain ":assumed-role:" in the plan.
sam: 👍 and mention `aws:SourceIdentity` caveat so future migrations don't hit this.
maria: Will do. Closing thread.
